findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. The memory check only runs through machine.join(). Direct `forge test --pytest <base>` instead reaches src/forge/fasttest.py:269 and launches pytest at :428 without joining, so it starts even below the memory floor. The named small-test proof invokes bare `forge test` (tests/test_machine_memory_budget.py:116), whose outer admission hides this bypass. Gate standalone picker runs while preserving execution inside an already admitted test command.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. On eight cores with two busy runners, a standalone `forge test` using `test = "pytest -n 4"` and no fast_test computes a two-process budget but still launches four workers. src/forge/review.py:488-492 only adds --maxprocesses when FORGE_TEST_CPUS already exists in the parent environment. The exported PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS affects automatic counts, not explicit -n values ([xdist contract](https://pytest-xdist.readthedocs.io/en/stable/distribution.html)). Runner reservations therefore go unenforced, while review.py:507 records two processes and doctor understates usage. The runner proof checks environment values in a script rather than the actual worker count.
